draft.title: Working as a team
card: A collaborative investigation is done by a group, so how the group works is part of the task. The group plans, collects data and reports together.
Sharing roles
each member takes a clear job, such as running the test, recording results or timing. Jobs are agreed early so the work is shared fairly and nothing is missed.
Communicating
members share updates, listen to each other and say when they are stuck. Clear messages stop mistakes, such as two people recording the same result in different ways.
Reflecting
after the work, the group looks back at what went well and what to change. It asks how roles, communication and teamwork affected the investigation.
draft.remember: A good investigation needs shared roles, clear communication and a look back at how the team worked.

a.q: Which action is an example of a group reflecting on its teamwork?
opts: Discussing which roles worked well and what to change
Agreeing who will time each sprint before testing starts
Telling the group that the stopwatch has run out of battery
Recording each result on the shared sheet after every run
a.why: Reflecting means looking back at how the group worked and what to change next time. The other options are planning, communicating and recording, which happen while the work is under way.
a.clue: Reflecting happens after the work, looking back.

b.q: Jaya's group is testing whether a warm-up changes sprint times. Two members both time the same runs, and nobody records the results. Which change would best fix this problem?
opts: Agree separate roles for timing and recording at the start
Ask every member to time every run on their own
Ask the group to reflect on the results once they are in
Let members choose jobs as they go during the testing
b.why: The problem is that jobs were not clearly shared, so one task was doubled and another was missed. Agreeing separate roles early fixes this. Reflecting later may show the problem but does not stop it happening during the testing.
b.clue: Look for the fix that gives each job to a named person.

a.best: Discussing which roles worked well and what to change

b.best: Agree separate roles for timing and recording at the start

problems.detail: The why says all the other options 'happen while the work is under way', but agreeing who will time each sprint happens before testing starts, as the option itself says. It would be better to say they happen before or during the work, not after it.

check.summary: Both questions have one clear right answer that matches the card. One small problem: the why for (a) says planning happens while the work is under way, when that option is set before testing starts.
